Concrete Slab Calculator

Free concrete calculator: enter slab length, width and thickness to get cubic yards, cubic feet and the number of 40, 60 or 80 lb bags needed.

Your estimate

Results update as you type. Round up when ordering.

Based on premixed concrete bags (e.g. Quikrete, Sakrete): 80 lb ≈ 0.60 cu ft, 60 lb ≈ 0.45, 40 lb ≈ 0.30. Brands vary slightly — check the label.

How to calculate concrete for a slab

Concrete is ordered by volume. Multiply length × width × thickness, keeping every measurement in feet (divide inches by 12). That gives cubic feet; divide by 27 to get cubic yards, the unit ready-mix suppliers use.

Example: a 10 × 10 ft patio, 4 in thick: 10 × 10 × 0.333 = 33.3 cu ft ÷ 27 = 1.23 cu yd. Adding 10% waste gives about 1.36 cu yd.

Bags vs. ready-mix truck

Typical pre-mixed bag yields: 80 lb ≈ 0.60 cu ft, 60 lb ≈ 0.45 cu ft, 40 lb ≈ 0.30 cu ft (check your bag label—yields vary slightly by brand). For jobs over about 1 cubic yard (45 × 80 lb bags), a ready-mix delivery is usually cheaper and gives a more uniform pour.

Recommended thickness

  • Walkways and patios: 4 in
  • Driveways for passenger cars: 4–5 in; heavier vehicles: 6 in
  • Shed bases: 4 in, thickened at the edges

Why add waste?

Uneven subgrade, form flex and spillage commonly consume 5–10% extra. Running short mid-pour creates a cold joint, so it is cheaper to order a little more.
